name: China
traditionNote: Codified, statute-first law with no binding precedent: you look for the enacted text and its implementing regulations first, and courts follow Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations and designated guiding cases rather than ordinary judgments.
summary: Laws (法律) are passed by the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee, promulgated by presidential order, and published in the Gazette of the NPC Standing Committee and on the NPC website; under the Legislation Law the text printed in that Gazette is the standard text. Administrative regulations (行政法规) are issued by the State Council and published in the State Council Gazette on gov.cn, which restates the same rule for its own contents, with department rules and local government rules published by their issuing bodies and collected in the national rules database. Each instrument states its own commencement date. The single most useful consolidated entry point is the official National Database of Laws and Regulations at flk.npc.gov.cn, run by the NPC Standing Committee, which carries the Constitution, laws, administrative regulations, supervisory regulations, local regulations and judicial interpretations, each with a scanned gazette PDF alongside the HTML. Only the Chinese text is authentic — every English version, including the NPC's own, is a reference translation.
hierarchy: Laws of the NPC and its Standing Committee (法律), including legislative interpretations
Administrative regulations of the State Council (行政法规)
Supervisory regulations of the National Supervisory Commission (监察法规)
Local regulations, autonomous regulations and separate regulations (地方性法规、自治条例、单行条例)
Department rules and local government rules (部门规章、地方政府规章)
Judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (司法解释), binding on courts and procuratorates

gazette.name: Quanguo Renmin Daibiao Dahui Changwu Weiyuanhui Gongbao
gazette.native: 中华人民共和国全国人民代表大会常务委员会公报
gazette.en: Gazette of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
gazette.authority: General Office of the NPC Standing Committee (全国人大常委会办公厅)
gazette.coverage: Full-issue PDFs of NPCSC Gazette numbers from 2018 to the current issue, roughly six or seven numbers a year, plus special issues such as the 2020 Civil Code, 2021 Criminal Law and 2026 Ecological and Environmental Code editions. Issues before 2018 are not on this index — the old /zgrdw/wxzl/gongbao/ archive path no longer serves a listing.
gazette.desc: The publication of record for national laws: it carries the texts of laws, legislative interpretations, decisions and resolutions of the NPC and its Standing Committee, appointment lists, and the annual work reports of the State Council, the National Supervisory Commission, the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate. Under the Legislation Law the text of a law as printed here is the standard text.
gazette.howto: The index is a flat list of year-and-issue links (2026年第四号, 2026年生态环境法典特刊, and so on) and each link opens a PDF of the whole issue directly — there is no per-issue HTML table of contents, so use the PDF's own contents page to find the presidential order and the law under it. The 更多>> link at http://www.npc.gov.cn/wxzlhgb/ccc/ shows the same 2018-onward run. To go straight to a named law instead, find it in flk.npc.gov.cn and open the scanned gazette file attached to the record.
gazette.note: npc.gov.cn is served over plain HTTP only; https://www.npc.gov.cn/ does not complete a TLS handshake at all, so the http:// address is the one that works.

constitution.name: Zhonghua Renmin Gongheguo Xianfa
constitution.en: Constitution of the People's Republic of China
constitution.authority: General Office of the NPC Standing Committee (全国人大常委会办公厅)
constitution.coverage: The consolidated operative text, 中华人民共和国宪法（2018年修正文本）, promulgated and in force 11 March 2018, being the 1982 Constitution as amended in 1988, 1993, 1999, 2004 and 2018. The original 1982 text and all five amendment acts are attached to the record as related documents.
constitution.desc: The Constitution's record in the official national database. It holds the consolidated 2018 amended text, and links from it to the 1982 original and to each constitutional amendment act separately, so you can see exactly what a given round changed. Downloads include a Word/OFD version and a scanned image of the gazette printing.
constitution.howto: Open the record and read the consolidated text; use the 相关文件 (related documents) panel for the 1982 Constitution and the 1988, 1993, 1999, 2004 and 2018 amendment acts, and the download control for the Word/OFD file or the scanned PDF. A plain HTML copy of the same 2018 text, easier to read or quote from, sits on the central government portal at https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2018-03/22/content_5276318.htm.
constitution.note: The database is a JavaScript application, so this record needs a real browser; the old https://flk.npc.gov.cn/xf.html constitution section page no longer exists. An English rendering is published by the NPC at http://en.npc.gov.cn.cdurl.cn/constitution.html, but it is a reference translation only — the Chinese text governs.

sources.name: Guojia Falu Fagui Shujuku
sources.en: National Database of Laws and Regulations
sources.authority: General Office of the NPC Standing Committee (全国人大常委会办公厅)
sources.coverage: Launched February 2021. Live category counts checked August 2026: 1 constitution record, 310 laws, 608 State Council administrative regulations, 2 supervisory regulations (监察法规), 561 judicial interpretations and 15,781 local, autonomous and separate regulations.
sources.desc: The state's own consolidated database and the default place to read the current text of any national law. Records carry both a searchable HTML and word-processor version and a scanned image of the gazette printing, so you can check the electronic text against the authoritative one in a single record.
sources.howto: The site has been rebuilt as a single-page application and the old section pages (/fl.html, /xzfg.html, /dfxfg.html, /sfjs.html) are gone, so start from the search box on the home page or from 高级检索 at https://flk.npc.gov.cn/advanceSearch. Narrow results with the 法律法规分类 (category), 时效性 (still in force or not), 制定机关 (enacting body) and 公布年份 facets, and the 精确/模糊 exact-versus-fuzzy toggle. Each record opens at /detail?id=<record id> with the text, a 相关文件 panel of amendments and related instruments, and downloads for the Word/OFD file and the scanned gazette PDF.
sources.note: It does not include State Council department rules or local government rules — the home page links out to the National Database of Rules on gov.cn for those. Category browsing has no URL of its own: filters live inside the application, so only /detail?id= record links can be bookmarked or cited.

sources.name: Zhonghua Renmin Gongheguo Guowuyuan Gongbao
sources.native: 中华人民共和国国务院公报
sources.authority: General Office of the State Council (国务院办公厅), on the central government portal gov.cn
sources.coverage: Founded by decision of a State Council executive meeting in 1955; current issues published by year and issue number, roughly three a month, with a separate 1954-1999 historical collection browsable year by year.
sources.desc: The gazette of record for the executive branch: administrative regulations, State Council decisions and orders, machinery-of-government and administrative-division changes, senior appointments and removals, and important department rules and documents. This is where an administrative regulation is formally promulgated, and the gazette states on its own pages that under the Legislation Law the regulation and rule texts printed here are the standard texts.
sources.howto: https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/ is a JavaScript redirect chain that lands on the current issue (for example https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12906/). From an issue page use 上一号 and 下一号 to step between numbers, 目录 for that issue's contents, and 公报搜索/高级搜索 for a title or full-text search across issues; the historical run 1954-1999 is linked from the same page and at https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/gongbao/guowuyuan1954_1999/.
sources.note: Only index and issue-level paths are served: the year-level directory https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/ returns HTTP 403. The redirect from /gongbao/ is script-driven, so text-only clients see an empty page and need the issue URL directly.

sources.name: Guojia Xingzheng Fagui Ku
sources.authority: Ministry of Justice (司法部), published in step with the central government portal gov.cn
sources.coverage: 608 State Council administrative regulations currently in force (live count, August 2026), reaching back to 1950, compiled as official versions under the Regulations on Procedures for Formulating Administrative Regulations and updated on an ongoing basis.
sources.desc: The Ministry of Justice's dedicated collection of State Council administrative regulations. Use it when you want the regulation layer on its own rather than filtered out of a mixed database: entries show the promulgation and commencement dates side by side and flag regulations that have an earlier-version history.
sources.howto: The root bounces by script to the title-search view at https://xzfg.moj.gov.cn/search2.html; from there switch between the 标题检索, 正文检索 and 高级检索 tabs, the last at https://xzfg.moj.gov.cn/SearchAdvancedFront, which adds 公布文号, 公布日期 and 施行日期 filters. Each hit carries a 历史沿革 link where earlier versions exist and 下载 buttons for a text version (Word) and an image version (PDF). The same collection is mirrored on the government portal at https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/xzfgk/.
sources.note: Chinese-only interface. The results lists are server-rendered and read fine in a text client, but the landing page redirects via JavaScript, so request /search2.html or /SearchAdvancedFront directly.

sources.name: Guojia Guizhang Ku
sources.authority: Central government portal (中国政府网) jointly with the Ministry of Justice, published in step with 中国政府法制信息网
sources.coverage: Department rules (部门规章) of State Council ministries, commissions, the People's Bank of China, the Audit Office and directly subordinate bodies with administrative functions, sourced from their websites and the State Council Gazette, plus local government rules (地方政府规章) from provincial, autonomous-region, municipality, districted-city and autonomous-prefecture governments and their gazettes — all currently in force, dynamically updated.
sources.desc: The layer the NPC database deliberately omits, and the flk home page links out to it for exactly that reason. If the instrument you need is a ministry 规章 or a provincial or municipal government 规章 rather than a law or an administrative regulation, this is where the official version lives.
sources.howto: Pick 全部规章, 部门规章 or 地方政府规章 from the tabs, then narrow with the 部门 filter and the 目录导航 tree. The search box lets you choose 标题 or 全文 as the search position, sort 按相关度 or 按时间, and filter by 一月内 / 一年内 / 不限; results link to the official compiled version of each rule.
sources.note: The site's own 说明 states that the texts here are the 国家正式版本 compiled by each issuing body to a uniform format under the Regulations on the Administration of the Editing and Publication of Compilations of Laws and Regulations.

sources.name: Zhongguo Renda Wang - Quanwei Fabu
sources.native: 中国人大网 权威发布
sources.authority: General Office of the NPC Standing Committee (全国人大常委会办公厅)
sources.coverage: Newly adopted laws, decisions and resolutions, presidential orders (主席令), NPCSC announcements and appointment and removal lists, released session by session, each law typically accompanied by its drafting explanation and the Constitution and Law Committee's review reports.
sources.desc: The NPC's own first-publication channel, named alongside the Gazette in the Legislation Law. It is the fastest official place to read a law the day it passes, before consolidated databases catch up, together with the drafting explanations and committee review reports that accompany it.
sources.howto: Open 法律文件 at http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c12435/c12488/ for statute texts, presidential orders and the accompanying explanations and review reports, or 决议决定 at http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c12435/c12489/ for decisions and resolutions; items are listed newest first and cluster by session date, so a law and its explanatory documents share one date.
sources.note: Plain HTTP only — the https:// form of npc.gov.cn does not complete a TLS handshake.

sources.name: Zuigao Renmin Fayuan - Sifa Jieshi
sources.native: 最高人民法院 司法解释
sources.authority: Supreme People's Court (最高人民法院)
sources.coverage: 400 items in the listing (live count, August 2026), newest first, covering interpretations, provisions (规定), replies (批复) and decisions on how statutes are applied, including joint 两高 instruments issued with the Supreme People's Procuratorate.
sources.desc: Judicial interpretations bind every court in China and in practice supply the operative detail that statutes leave open, so a statute read without its interpretations is only half the rule. This is the SPC's own release page for them, under 权威发布 > 司法解释.
sources.howto: Page through the listing newest-first with the 首页/上一页/下一页/尾页 controls, or use the site search at www.court.gov.cn with the interpretation's title keywords. For consolidated older interpretations, search the 司法解释 category in flk.npc.gov.cn, which holds 561 of them with gazette scans.

sources.name: Zuigao Renmin Fayuan - Zhidaoxing Anli
sources.native: 最高人民法院 指导性案例
sources.authority: Supreme People's Court (最高人民法院)
sources.coverage: 206 items in the listing (live count, August 2026), running through the numbered batches to batch 49 and guiding case No. 279, released February 2026.
sources.desc: Guiding cases are the closest thing China has to precedent: lower courts are expected to refer to them when deciding similar matters. Each entry gives the key point, the facts and the reasoning in a standardised form, and party names are anonymised to a surname plus 某.
sources.howto: Browse the listing newest-first — entries are titled 指导性案例NNN号 so batches sit together by release date — or search the case name. The same cases are reproduced in the Supreme People's Court Gazette, whose 指导性案例 column at http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/ArticleList.html?serial_no=al lists them with the issue they appeared in, and in the People's Court Case Database.

sources.name: Renmin Fayuan Anli Ku
sources.authority: Supreme People's Court (最高人民法院)
sources.coverage: Opened to the public 27 February 2024 with 3,711 cases; 3,927 cases as of August 2026, split between 指导性案例 and 参考案例 and grouped as criminal, civil, administrative, state-compensation and enforcement, with a separate 多元解纷案例库 of dispute-resolution cases alongside it.
sources.desc: A curated database of cases the Supreme People's Court has reviewed and considers to have reference value for similar disputes. Since judgment publication on China Judgements Online has contracted, this is now the most reliable official window onto how courts actually decide.
sources.howto: Search across 全文, 标题, 案例编号, 裁判日期, 关键词, 基本案情 or 裁判理由, then open 高级检索 to filter by 案由, 案件类型, 审理程序, 审理法院, 法院级别 and 文书类型, with a 精确检索 / 模糊检索 toggle and a 结果中检索 option to search within results. An account is only needed for bookmarks, notes and feedback, not for reading.
sources.note: It is a selection, not a record of litigation — cases are here because the SPC chose them, so absence of a case proves nothing.

sources.name: Zhongguo Caipan Wenshu Wang
sources.authority: Supreme People's Court (最高人民法院)
sources.coverage: Judgment documents uploaded by courts nationwide from 2013 onward, browsable as 刑事/民事/行政/赔偿/执行 and other categories, plus a 民族语言文书 section in Mongolian, Tibetan, Uyghur, Korean and Kazakh; upload volumes have fallen sharply since 2021.
sources.desc: The mass repository of individual court judgments and rulings — still the only place to look for an ordinary decision by a named party or case number, even in its diminished state.
sources.howto: Search by case number (案号), party name or cause of action, or narrow first with the case-category tabs and 高级检索. Registration has required mobile-phone verification since 1 September 2020, and querying or downloading needs you to be logged in; the front page currently carries a standing notice that data updates are running late because of a technical fault, so check it when results look empty.
sources.note: From August 2023 many courts stopped uploading and large numbers of previously published documents were taken down; a separate internal 全国法院裁判文书库 launched in January 2024 is available only to court staff on the judicial intranet, so this site is not a complete record of decided cases.

sources.name: Zuigao Renmin Fayuan Gongbao
sources.native: 中华人民共和国最高人民法院公报
sources.en: Gazette of the Supreme People's Court
sources.authority: Supreme People's Court (最高人民法院), edited by the General Office of the SPC
sources.coverage: Monthly issues with back issues browsable year by year from 1985 to the current 2026 volume, organised into columns including 法律法规, 司法解释, 司法文件, 任免事项, 司法统计, 指导性案例, 裁判文书选登 and 案例.
sources.desc: The court's official periodical, carrying judicial interpretations, selected judgments (裁判文书选登) and guiding cases in their authoritative published form. Gazette cases carry more weight in practice than an ordinary judgment pulled from the judgments site.
sources.howto: Use 公报过刊 at http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/PeriodicalsDic.html to pick a year and issue — note that some issues expose the table of contents only — or use the 公报检索 form on that page to search by 标题, 全文 or 文号 and restrict to a 栏目 such as 指导性案例 or 裁判文书选登. The guiding-case series alone is at http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/ArticleList.html?serial_no=al.
sources.note: HTTP only: https://gongbao.court.gov.cn/ returns HTTP 502 every time, so use the http:// address. Even over http the server intermittently returns 502 on individual pages — retry rather than assuming the page is gone.

sources.name: Zhonghua Renmin Gongheguo Tiaoyue Shujuku
sources.native: 中华人民共和国条约数据库
sources.en: Treaty Database of the People's Republic of China
sources.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (外交部), Department of Treaty and Law
sources.coverage: Bilateral and multilateral treaties drawn from the ministry's own 《中华人民共和国条约集》 (compiled since 1957) and 《中华人民共和国多边条约集》 (since 1986), plus more recently concluded or acceded-to treaties, treaties for which China is the depositary, and some bilateral cooperation documents. Treaties that have lapsed are deliberately retained for research.
sources.desc: The foreign ministry's own treaty register, and the official starting point for whether China is party to an instrument and on what terms. Built under the Law on the Procedure for the Conclusion of Treaties, which puts the ministry in charge of treaty-making work under the State Council.
sources.howto: Browse the 全部 / 双边 / 多边 tabs, or the separate list of multilateral treaties for which China is depositary, and use 高级搜索 to search by title, counterpart country or date; records open as detail pages (web/detail1.jsp?objid=...) with the text and treaty particulars. The ministry also lists treaty status summaries at https://www.mfa.gov.cn/wjb_673085/zfxxgk_674865/gknrlb/tywj/tyqk/.
sources.note: Chinese-language interface, and the ministry's own front-page disclaimer says it cannot guarantee that the database text matches the formal treaty text and accepts no liability for reliance on it — so verify against the instrument itself. A treaty's authentic languages are those stated in the instrument.

sources.name: National People's Congress English site - Laws
sources.authority: General Office of the NPC Standing Committee (全国人大常委会办公厅)
sources.coverage: A selective and slowly growing set of English translations of national laws — the page is headed 'Laws (Translation for Reference Only)' — plus the Constitution and legislative-process material.
sources.desc: The only English texts of Chinese national laws published by the legislature itself. Useful as the least-bad English starting point, and for the NPC's own English account of how legislation is made.
sources.howto: Laws sits under Resources in the top navigation and Legislation under Our Work; the Constitution is its own top-level item at /constitution.html. There is no search over the translations, so scroll the Laws list.
sources.note: Reference translations only — no English version is authentic and coverage is patchy. The domain deserves a word: en.npc.gov.cn does not resolve from outside China, and http://www.npc.gov.cn/englishnpc/ redirects here, which is what backs the official flag. cdurl.cn is a Wangsu/ChinaNetCenter CDN edge that presents a shared certificate for default.chinanetcenter.com, so https:// fails and the http:// address is the one that works.

sources.name: China Law Translate
sources.coverage: Laws, draft laws, regulations, judicial interpretations and policy documents, chosen for topicality rather than completeness, indexed by topic and by issuing body (SPC, SPP, State Council, MPS, MOJ and others).
sources.desc: An independent, crowd-sourced translation project widely relied on by researchers because it often publishes readable English of a new law or draft well before any official version exists.
sources.howto: Search the English title, or browse the Topics and Departments menus; the References section adds standing aids such as a criminal-procedure timetable, a sentencing guide and a list of civil causes of action. Translations are dated and usually paired with the Chinese source text.
sources.note: Unofficial. Not a government publication and carries no legal status; check the date, since translations are of the version current when posted.

sources.name: NPC Observer
sources.authority: Independent project by Changhao Wei and Taige Hu
sources.coverage: NPC and NPCSC sessions from the 12th NPC (2013) to the current one, bills and drafts open for public comment, legislative calendars, commencement dates, oversight reports, and dedicated pages for Hong Kong-related NPC and NPCSC decisions and interpretations.
sources.desc: The clearest English tracking of what the legislature is actually doing: which bills are moving, when a law takes effect, what is out for public comment. It is the practical index to the official sources rather than a substitute for them.
sources.howto: Use the Legislation menu for texts and status by category (national laws, legislative interpretations and so on) or by NPC term, and the Sessions pages and Session Watch posts for what is scheduled next; each entry links back to the official Chinese source.
sources.note: Unofficial. Excellent and free, with optional paid newsletter support, but it is commentary and tracking, not an authoritative text.

sources.name: Beida Fabao (PKULaw / Chinalawinfo)
sources.authority: Chinalawinfo Co., originating from Peking University (founded 1985)
sources.coverage: Central and local legislation from 1949 to present — the publisher claims over 4.6 million legislative documents — plus judicial cases, judicial interpretations, legislative history, treaties and Hong Kong/Macao/Taiwan material, and thousands of English translations.
sources.desc: The commercial database Chinese practitioners and law libraries actually use, because it links amendments, superseded versions, related rules and cases in a way the official databases do not. Its English translation library is the largest available anywhere.
sources.howto: Search by title or citation in the laws-and-regulations module and use the version history and related-documents panels on a record; most access is via an institutional subscription.
sources.note: Unofficial and paywalled, and the translations carry no legal status. Both en.pkulaw.com and the Chinese-side www.pkulaw.com load from outside China, but full records need an institutional or paid login.

findLaw.task: Find the current text of a national law
findLaw.steps: Search the exact Chinese title, e.g. 中华人民共和国民法典, in the National Database of Laws and Regulations, then narrow with the 法律法规分类 facet set to 法律 and 时效性 set to in force. Open the record and download either the Word/OFD file or the scanned gazette PDF. Note the old /fl.html section page no longer exists — search, then filter.

findLaw.task: See what a recent amendment changed, and when it takes effect
findLaw.steps: Open the law's record in the national database and use its 相关文件 panel, which lists the amending acts and earlier versions, then read the amending decision itself in the NPC Standing Committee Gazette or in 法律文件 on the NPC site, where the drafting explanation and the Constitution and Law Committee's review report set out the changes article by article.

findLaw.task: Find subordinate legislation: an administrative regulation or a ministry rule
findLaw.steps: For a State Council administrative regulation (行政法规) use the Ministry of Justice database's title or advanced search, or the mirrored collection on gov.cn. For a ministry or local government rule (规章), which those collections omit, use the National Database of Rules and pick the 部门规章 or 地方政府规章 tab, then filter by 部门 or by region.

findLaw.task: Find how courts apply a provision
findLaw.steps: Start with the judicial interpretation on point from the Supreme People's Court release page or the 司法解释 category in the national database, then look for vetted guiding and reference cases in the People's Court Case Database using 高级检索 to filter by 案由, 案件类型, 审理程序 and 法院级别.

findLaw.task: Look up a specific court decision by party or case number
findLaw.steps: Search the case number (案号) or party name on China Judgements Online; you will need a registered, phone-verified account to query or download. If nothing comes back, treat that as inconclusive rather than proof the case does not exist, and check the Supreme People's Court Gazette for selected judgments.

findLaw.task: Find a provincial or municipal regulation
findLaw.steps: Search the national database and set the 法律法规分类 facet to 地方法规, which holds 15,781 local, autonomous and separate regulations, then narrow by 制定机关 to the issuing people's congress. For local government rules rather than local regulations, switch to the National Database of Rules and use its 地方政府规章 tab.

subnational: Subnational legislation is substantial. Provincial-level people's congresses, and the congresses of larger and designated cities, enact local regulations (地方性法规); ethnic autonomous areas enact autonomous and separate regulations; provincial and municipal governments issue local government rules (地方政府规章). Each is promulgated locally in the issuing congress's or government's own gazette, but the national aggregation points are the 地方法规 category of flk.npc.gov.cn, holding 15,781 instruments, and the National Database of Rules on gov.cn for local government 规章, whose texts are drawn from provincial, autonomous-region, municipality, districted-city and autonomous-prefecture government sites and gazettes. The Hong Kong and Macao Special Administrative Regions run entirely separate legal systems with their own gazettes and legislation databases, and mainland databases do not carry their legislation.
caveats: Only the Chinese text is authoritative, and where the electronic and printed versions differ the standard text is the one printed in the relevant gazette — the NPC Standing Committee Gazette for laws, the State Council Gazette for administrative regulations and rules, a rule each gazette restates on its own pages — which is why flk.npc.gov.cn attaches scanned gazette images to its records. Every English version, including the NPC's own translations, is a reference rendering with no legal force, and coverage is selective and often years behind. Case law is the weakest link: China Judgements Online was never complete, upload volumes fell steeply after 2021, many previously published documents were removed, and the replacement 全国法院裁判文书库 launched in 2024 is an internal system available only to court personnel, so a search returning nothing tells you nothing. The official sites are also awkward to reach and cite: npc.gov.cn and the Supreme People's Court Gazette serve plain HTTP only, the NPC English site resolves only through a commercial CDN hostname, gov.cn returns 403 on some directory paths, and flk.npc.gov.cn has been rebuilt as a JavaScript application in which category listings have no stable URL and older section links such as /fl.html and /xf.html are dead. The databases have structural gaps too — the NPC database excludes department rules and local government rules — while the comprehensive consolidated products with version histories and English translations (北大法宝/PKULaw, Westlaw China and similar) are private and paywalled. Intra-Party regulations (党内法规) form a parallel normative system that none of these state legal databases collect.
